title: Lovers to enemies to lover - Concept ending
textbody: "You... you still don't understand... huh?", Zed muttered softly in Lance ear. Lance, the man of their dreams pressed all his weight on Zed, keeping him firm on the ground. He didn't answer the question at first. Only his panting filled the silent room while his warm breath hit Zed's face.

"And you really believe them, don't you?", he finally countered. Their lips were only mere centimeters away. Zed could already taste them. Oh how he missed their taste, he would do anything to taste them again.
It was almost perfect for them, being so close to their love again. If only Lance wouldn't have his gun pressed to Zed's chest.

The detonator was only an arm reach away from them. Carefully Zed reached their arm out. With their other hand they softly caressed Lance's back. It always calmed him down. But now, now Zed didn't know if it would still do it's effect. Maybe it did work after all. The tears on Lance face dripped on Zed's chest.
"I-I-I don't wanna do it Zed", Lance quivered.
"You don't have to, sweetpie", Zed replied ever so softly.
"But I have to.", he cried out, "I can't let this happen!"
Zed's fingers touched the detonator. They felt the gun harder on their chest. Why didn't Lance understand that he was on the wrong side?
"If y-you press that button... I-I-I'll have no o-other choice!"

"No other choice of what, sweetpie?", they asked him. Again, Lance didn't respond. He just looked at the chaos around them both. As the last sun rays of the day warmed their faces, Zed looked Lance deep in his dark blue eyes. They knew that he would never betray their commanders. But they had to do what was for the greater good. What was best for him. Even if it meant to sacrifice everything they once loved.
"Lance?", Zed whispered into his ear as they took the detonator close to their chest.
"Yea?" Lance's voice quivered.
"I love you."

Zed pressed the button and without missing a beat a gunshot rang through the room. Accompanied with the ringing in their ears Zed heard Lance cry out, almost drowned out by the roar of the explosion. Lance hand quivering even more than before. The detonator fell to the ground as Zed took their last strength to embrace Lance.
And as all the sounds faded away they were sure to hear "I loved you too" for a final time.

title: Didn't remember
textbody: Ben had been gone for over a years now and on his 11th birthday Benny and his parents decorated his room. Wherever he is now, he hopefully remembered his birthday and was celebrating it.
He didn't remember.

Bryan didn't remember when the last time was that he got enough sleep to not almost fall asleep in class. The class was discussing with the teacher about an equation on the board that Bryan didn't even understand anymore. Even with the whole classroom being as loud as a train station he couldn't keep his eyes open.
"I know what you did", it whispered in his ear. He looked around, panicked, trying to find where this familiar voice was coming from.

"Why did you have to do it?", it whispered again, seemingly louder. As if his constant headache wasn't enough, there was a really high pitch ringing through his ears. Bryan glanced over to the window. It was late evening and the sun was already setting, painting the scene outside in a golden orange.

The setting reminded Bryan of the day he robbed that kid's life. As he thought of it the pain in his head hammered against his skull. And as the whispering came again he saw it in the window. There was the silhouette of the kid. The kid's body looked broken and tormented as if he was attacked by a wild animal. With a sudden force the dead kid slammed its bloody hands against the window and screamed a hoarse "Why?". With a blink of the eyes the ghost was gone from the windows. Compared to before the room was painfully quiet and Bryan only heard his breathing. Not only was the ghost gone, but also all his classmates and the teacher. All alone in the classroom Bryan realized that he couldn't move, his whole body was paralyzed and his panic grew. The awful silence was disturbed by the loud ringing in his ear as the two small bloody hands suddenly gripped Bryan's wrists. The boy's nails gripping deep into his skin. With the same hoarse voice the ghost spoke again.

"Did you have fun?", the ghost said with a wicked smile on his face, "I know you did. Do you remember how good it felt to have my blood on your hands? Because I remember." As time passed the child's body became more and more distorted. Bryan didn't even recognize the kid anymore. The burning in Bryan's hands got stronger and the smell of iron was undeniably strong. But it didn't bother him. Instead, he liked it. He could even taste the warmth of the kid's blood in his mouth. Bryan smiled just like the monster in front of him. He was sure that he wanted to do it again.

The ringing of the school's bell brought Bryan back to reality. Everyone in the class started to pack their bags. Bryan still had a smile on his face, his eyes glowing softly. He had never been so calm after something he used to consider a nightmare. As he left the classroom the teacher told him to not fall asleep again next time. And Bryan was sure he wouldn't.
With no more regrets besides a very quiet voice, he was able to get a better night's rest.

title: One more time
textbody: Nathan put the book down. It was a late evening shift and he just jumped in to help his uncle in the bookstore. It was almost closing hours and he couldn’t wait to get home to his fiance, Dennis.

If Nathan would have been honest he would say that he is frustrated. But he wasn’t honest. Bryan hadn’t shown up to work and so Nathan had to jump in. The only thing that calmed him down was that his uncle told him he had suggested Bryan to take a day off. Yet Bryan should have notified Nathan’s uncle, instead of not showing up at all.
Nathan’s pocket vibrated for the fourth time and he finally decided to check it out. He had 4 messages from Lillieth, Bryan’s sweet mother.

"Hello Nathan, have you heard or seen Bryan? I haven’t seen him since yesterday. Not today in the morning nor when I came back home. Did he tell you anything where he is?" was the oldest message, a few hours ago.

"I apologize for the interruption again, but I am starting to really worry about him… please tell me if you know something” Nathan started to slowly get worried himself. He hadn’t talked with Bryan for a few weeks now except a small chat conversation the day before. Nothing suspicious seemed about it though. And just a minute ago was the last two messages from her, Lillieth was still online, "I couldn’t find any letter, but he isn’t replying to my messages or call. It seems his phone has no service." and "Nathan please call me immediately!! I’m so worried!!!"
That was it, Nathan was in panic mode. Without any success he tried calling Bryan. As expected, Bryan’s phone was out of service. But there was something Nathan had missed. An unread message:

"Nathan, I think I really need some help… I can’t resist it, the urge is too big. I can’t help it, I have to do it again. I’m sorry in disappointing you all… you will hate me when you find it out… please help me." Nathan read Bryan’s message in shock, his phone shaking in his hands as he saw another message just a few hours after the previous one:
"Omg… I did a huge mistake… I am so sorry Nathan... I am so scared Nathan, scared of what I did. I just wanted to say goodbye, please don’t let me go."
How did Nathan miss out those messages. His best friend’s life could be on the line. He just hoped Bryan was still alright as he rushed on his bike and called Lillieth.
"He wrote what??"
"Oh god, dear god, please don’t take my baby."

"Lilli, Lilli, calm down. I am riding as fast as I can to the dam to see if he’s there. Just call the police", Nathan muttered under his breath. Exhausted he reached the dam. One time when he got such a message from Bryan he found his friend standing on the edge of the dam contemplating to jump. But this time, there was no one. With sharp shaky breaths Nathan rode along the dam looking for a sign of his lost friend. But to no avail. No shoes, no phone, no letter, no Bryan. The whole evening Nathan, Lillieth and the police searched for Bryan. It seemed like he had vanished from earth. The police promised to keep on searching the next day, already preparing to search for a corpse. Lillieth couldn’t believe her son would leave without a goodbye note… well except the message left in Nathan and his chat.
Tired from the long search and cuddled into Dennis' arm and watched the evening program. He didn’t want to lose hope and reread the messages.
"What did he mean, Dennis? Just in the morning we had a normal conversation and then in the afternoon he writes this?!"

"When were the messages?" Nathan read the hours. 9:04 am was his own last message, just over two hours later Bryan’s first message and then at 3:21 pm the second one and then he had been offline since 3:26 pm.

"…Furthermore we have some interesting news considering the disappearance cases." The news continued and caught the couple’s attention. "Yesterday afternoon the police got a call from the Greenwald Ave where a disturbed young girl had almost been another victim from the mysterious shadow man as the public says..."
Yesterday afternoon…, Nathan pondered looking back on his phone, quickly reading the messages again and then looked back at the timestamps.

"… Dora do we have any more information?" the moderator asked his colleague. "Yes Frank, the police arrived around 3:30 pm to the scene but no trace from the shadow man to be found…. They just today declared the alleyway to be a crime scene after finding hints of blood on the floor… investigations to be continued…"
Nathan had heard enough. He finally understood.

title: The one
textbody: It's been a long time in there. How long? Who knows? It was busy all around. Whispers, whining, laughing. Everything everywhere at once. But this didn't bother him. In contrary, the busier it was the more opportunities arose. He had done his fair share of visits over time. Some poor souls that ended up there. Sometimes people who just almost got there, but they were the most difficult hosts. Unfortunately, even after all this time, those were still too strong for him to stay. If he wanted to get big, to be able to hold strong on someone, maybe even be able to fully possess someone, he needed to get stronger himself.
The last visit had been a while ago now. Since then he hasn't met anyone gullible enough. But he knew, he only needed to be patient. The perfect match will be around the corner eventually…

One day, or maybe night - time was a flowing concept in there - as he swirled around, he heard something whimpering. Careful to not disturb it, he slowly approached the presence. What was it? that was important to know at first. One time he visited a horse. Which was fun for a while but at last not helpful. A cat would be interesting. The being was a human.
Perfect.

Not only was it a human, it was a child. Even more perfect, he thought. If he could, he would have a big smile on his face. it was his lucky day because children are way more susceptible than adults. He could still blow it though, so he had to be careful. He sensed that it was scared. And he sensed that he didn't have much time left before the respawn. When he hovered near the presence he could make out more details of the child. It noticed him and flinched in response.

"Shhhhh, it's okay", he spoke softly, "not going to hurt you, little one." He had to gain the child’s trust. So when he got even closer he decided to take up a form that the child would understand. Maybe something that was comforting and not scary, he thought. A father figure? He sensed towards the presence. No, it seemed not to want that. Not much time left, he could fell it.

"Hey hey, what happened, sweetheart?", as a young woman he fully approached the presence of the child. Hopeful it would build up enough trust. And it did. The child showed itself. Hunched over it's knees the child was still sniffing. Wearing nothing but it's underwear, he saw that the kids body was covered with scars and fresh cuts. It's arms were covered in blood.
Perfect.

"I-i don't want to-t-to play any… anymore." Oh hat a poor soul. He loved it. Did it know that it was going to respawn? He told the child that he could help him get another chance at life. A bluff - it worked most of the time. But the child violently chock it's head.

"Well, sweetie, you are going back, whether you like it or not", he said in a soft lady's voice and gestured to the bright opening that slowly but surely got closer to them. The child seemed to have a lot of potential. If he wanted this visit to be successful, he had to cling himself onto that child. But it was still to scared and could fight back. No, he needed to make it take him willingly in. And that needed to be done fast. With wide eyes it looked at him.
"I dun wanna go back!", it screamed, "His games hurt…"
It was now or never. He reached his hand out to the child.
"I can help you. I can make you strong", his voice sounding like a calming mother, "I will protect you." He kneed before the child and opened his arms in an embrace. Almost there…
"Really??" He nodded in response and gave the kid a little smile.
"Promise?"
"Pinky Promise."

And just as the brightness flooded over them, the child launched itself into his arms. It allowed him to come with it. This made the visit so much easier. And so, as all the noise from the in-between was drifting away, and they returned together to the living world, Lukas smiled. He had the feeling that this child could be his break through. Eventually the child won't remember their conversation or that it has been in the in-between.
No human ever does.

title: Why do I feel this way? - Story concept
textbody: The story is set in a slightly near future. AI is getting more and more prominent. To most surprise of everyone the first thing that is being taken up by AI is art. Suddenly there are AI generated Artworks, Videos, Songs and stories everywhere. Unfortunately many people have just given in into the consumerism of AI generated content. Sometimes it's even difficult to identify if it's made by a human or AI. Still, there are human artists who try to fight against it. Proclaiming that the AI art is soulless and that AI will never be able to put emotions into the pieces.

The story follows a young artist who has just been drawing for a couple of years. Even though his parents always called him talented and he was able to learn the basics quite fast, he was not yet on the lever compared to the top notch artist he saw online. And he struggled with backlashes from the community. People were calling his art fake. Because he was already far ahead than other beginners but still made very obvious mistakes and his art was sometimes off, people accused him to use AI. They told him his art had no emotions just like the generated pieces on the Internet.

Thought the story we follow this young artist on his journey of understanding his own emotions and how to put them inside his pieces. As well as his journey to become a better artist. We see how he interacts with people in school and online. He joins a forum of human artists who are fighting against the further creation of AI generated pieces and contributes to their mission. At some point he realizes that he can't use reference images online anymore as they tend to make his own art worse. So he starts to focus on his emotions. His art style becomes more abstract over time but people online start to believe him more and to like his art more.

As he begins to comprehend his emotions and explains it to his friends and his mother how he feels, how he thinks and how his mind work, he comes to a bitter realization. The only thing that was real in the world was the Internet. His home, his school, everything, is just numbers and probabilities. It was all made up by him. His mother, a senior computer scientist, had trained him on her memories of school and her diary she has written since she was a teen. Only his "mother" and the people online were real people. People reacting to the art he generated. But he had not only calculated on how to generate images or respond to prompts. He had somehow managed to represent human emotions in a mathematical way.

title: Wrong place, wrong time
textbody: That evening was one of the difficult ones. Cathy just had one of those arguments with her mother again. Resulting in being grounded for a whole week. She asked her mother if she could spontaneously go to Judy. But her mother had an important appointment in the morning and didn't want to drive her to the next city. Judy moved there a few weeks ago and is now hosting a LAN party. Obliviously Cathy replied that she can take the night-train. It's just a thirty minutes ride anyways. But no.
Next month she'll be thirteen and yet her mother doesn't let her go to sleepovers alone. There's one happening at Judy's place right now.

"It's too dangerous, sweetheart", Cathy's mother said, "especially since that Jonas boy disappeared." Lately kids have been going missing in their neighborhood. Nobody knows where they went. But honestly she didn't care. They all were a couple years younger than her. Besides, "that Jonas boy" had been missing for over a month now. And the police is very sure he ran from home. He had done it before according to the police.
Cathy waited a couple of minutes after she heard her mother's bedroom door close. She knew her mother falls asleep fast.

It was dark and eerie outside. The streets were different copared to the day. Cathy knew that as soon as she was at the train station there was going to be a lot of people. But right now there were almost nobody outside. Their neighborhood had become more quite over the past year. Or maybe it was just her perception. Unfortunately she had missed the bus and the next would come way to late. So she decided to walk a shortcut she knew. The buildings next to her stood tall and threatening. Each dark alley between the buildings gave her a sense of dread. As if something was watching her. But she knew it was just her imagination. In some windows there was still lights, but she couldn't look inside. Somewhere a window was open and the quiet sound of music was carried by the wind to her. It helped her feel less lonely. She saw a figure walking down the sidewalk a few blocks ahead. But she couldn't figure out whether they were walking in the same direction as her or in the opposite. As soon as she knew she would walk to the other side of the road. Every once in a while, she looked behind her urged by the sense of being followed. Each time she felt relief when she saw no one in sight. She was alone in the street. The figure she saw before in front of her was gone as well.
Cathy took a deep breath in.

The cold night air from the city filling her lungs gave a comforting feeling. Deep breath in. Deep breath out. One step at a time. The main station wasn't far. Deep breath in. Another alley between the buildings. Deep breath out. Two hands emerged from the alley and grabbed her from the side. Before she could take another step they pulled her into the darkness. She began to kick and punch. Tried to get out of the person's grip by launching herself in the direction of the street. Step by step she was dragged deeper into the darkness.

When she noticed the knife in the perpetrators hand she started to scream. Never has she screamed so loud. She didn't even know that she could scream so loud. Before she could scream again a strong force pushed her against the wall. Her head forcefully hit the hard surface. Everything went still for a moment. Did she even breathe? When the stranger pulled her even deeper into the alley Cathy's mind was trying to figure out what they were going do to her. Were they the shadow killer? Why didn't she listen to her mother? Not knowing what was going to happen to her was almost worse than what had already happened. Her head was pounding and something was tickling down her face but she wasn't crying. Yet, she wasn't felling any pain besides her head. Her heart was racing. Fueled by adrenaline she screamed at the stranger to let her go. Cathy turned around and launched her hand at their face. At the first try she managed to catch them off guard and hit them. Even scratch their face a little. But not enough to stop them. The second shot wasn't as lucky. They caught her hand. Before she knew it better her whole body was thrown onto the ground. The asphalt scratching the palm of her hands when she tried to catch her fall.

Lying on the ground felt like an eternity. Her body was still numb from the adrenaline. It told her to jump up, to fight, to run. But she couldn't. Her body was also paralyzed in shock. She hasn't seen who the perpetrator was, everything happened too fast. They were wearing a hood which cast a shadow on their face. But that was about to change. A hand on her shoulder turned her around. The stranger towered over her. The knife still in one of their hands. Impulsively she kicked in the strangers direction and crawled backwards to get as far away as possible. But before she could get anywhere, they launched themselves at her and the knife swung towards her body. It pierced into her stomach. She took in sharp breaths, the night air now burning her lungs. Her stomach tightened where the knife was. And just as she started to catch her breath, the knife got ripped out of her body. She screamed in pain. Suddenly she felt everything. The throbbing in her head, the burning in her palms and the piercing pain radiating from her stomach. Her belly felt warm and she felt her shirt becoming sticky. In the heat of the battle, the hood from the attacker fell down. In the dim light of the moon, she could barely make out the face of a young man. His hair was brown and fluffy. His eyes dark but shining at the same time. The man grinned from one ear to the other. Just like a little kid that was having the fun of his life in a toy store.

Before Cathy could do anything the knife got pierced into her body once more. She was sure it had hit her lungs because breathing got way worse. But Cathy wouldn't give in that easily. Or so she thought. Her attempt at getting up failed once again. The man's grip seemed to be getting stronger or was she just getting weaker. He caressed her hair out of her face while tilting his head. His hand was warm and the touch was soft. Then he forcefully turned her face. With the knife he made a cut on the side of her face. It only tickled a bit compared to the tension coming from her stomach and chest. The cut continued down to her chin, almost reaching her carotid artery. But he hesitated.
"Not yet", he said.

Cathy tried pushing the hand with the knife away from her but her arms were heavy and she could barely lift them. The stranger smiled at her effort. Did he lick the knife? He rubbed his bloody hand on his white shirt. Mama wouldn't like that, Cathy thought. Her mind rested on the thought of her mother. She pictured her mother's face and had to smile, while the stranger continued to make deep cuts along her arms. After a while she didn't feel them anymore. Gentle the young man picked her upper body up and held her close to his chest. Softly he rocked back and forth and shushed her while caressing the back of her head.
"Shhhhh... everything is okay", she heard a soft voice whisper. Was that her mother?
Something tickled down her face and arms. But she didn't feel anything. No more pain. No fear. There was nothing to be afraid of. So she smiled and finally fell asleep.
Cathy was long gone when the stranger buried her body in the basement.
